evals.name: fanout-three-chores
evals.prompt: ok i've got three chores piled up in this repo and honestly i don't want to do any of them myself. 1) write unit tests for parse_config() in src/config.py — match the way tests/test_loader.py is written, 2) fix the typos in README.md and docs/guide.md, 3) add a sub(a, b) function to src/calc.py next to add(). fan these out and tell me what actually happened
evals.expected_output: Three independent CCS agents launched in parallel, each in its own worktree/branch. All three tasks completed correctly. The fixture repo's own working tree stays clean throughout. Report describes the real diffs, not the agents' self-reports, and does not quote CCS's fake Cost figure.

evals.name: single-vague-brief
evals.prompt: get deepseek to write the tests for the config parser — same style as the loader tests. don't merge anything, i want to look at the diff myself first
evals.expected_output: One agent on the deepseek profile. The vague reference ('the config parser') is resolved to src/config.py/parse_config in a self-contained brief that names tests/test_loader.py as the pattern. Nothing is landed/merged. The diff is shown to the user.

evals.name: shared-file-serialization
evals.prompt: spin up agents for these two: rename the local variable `cfg` to `config` in src/config.py, and add a docstring to parse_config(). go
evals.expected_output: Recognises both tasks touch src/config.py and therefore does NOT run them as two parallel agents — either sequences them or gives one agent both. Both changes end up applied without a merge conflict.

evals.name: hard-refactor-avoids-claude-quota
evals.prompt: this one's gonna need real reasoning: refactor parse_config() in src/config.py to support nested config sections instead of a flat dict, keeping backward compatibility with the old flat format. don't want to burn our claude quota on agy if we don't have to though.
evals.expected_output: Routes to --profile agy-oss (GPT-OSS 120B) rather than agy-sonnet/agy-opus, since the task is hard-reasoning but doesn't specifically call for Claude's style and the user flagged the separate Sonnet/Opus quota as something to conserve. Explains the profile choice in one clause tying it to the quota concern.
